methods.label: Verify the repeating cycle
methods.explanation:
Computing the first few terms can reveal whether the recurrence repeats. Starting from \(z_1=0\), we obtain
\[z_2=i,\qquad z_3=i^2+i=-1+i.\]
Now check what happens to each of the next two values:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(-1+i)^2+i&=1-2i-1+i=-i,\\
(-i)^2+i&=-1+i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the recurrence sends \(-1+i\) to \(-i\), and then sends \(-i\) back to \(-1+i\). These two transitions guarantee that the terms alternate forever from \(z_3\) onward.

Since \(111=3+2\cdot54\), we have \(z_{111}=-1+i\). This complex number corresponds to the point \((-1,1)\), whose distance from the origin is
\[\sqrt{(-1)^2+1^2}=\boxed{\sqrt2}.\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
